directions.title: Vector A
directions.prompt:
Use case: logo-brand.
Asset type: a professionally art-directed logo concept presentation for Astro90.com.
Brand context: Astro90 is the parent development studio behind Lighthouse, Inkube, Ktesio, Yanando, Heronis, and other products. It builds games, agentic AI software, and open-source software. The identity must have enough character for games and enough clarity for software and an umbrella studio.
Output: landscape 1536x1024 image, flat vector-like graphic design with crisp precise edges. Strictly black and white: solid black ink on pure white background. Restrained, original, confident identity design with generous white space and optically balanced proportions. This is a logo exploration, not a website or merchandise mockup.
Presentation layout: one generously sized main logo lockup centered in the upper 75 percent of the page. Along the bottom, present two discreet small-scale versions of the same emblem: solid black on white, and solid white on a solid black square. The small versions must reproduce the main emblem faithfully. Keep these supporting samples visually quiet and aligned. No headings, labels, explanatory text, slogans, color swatches, decorative lines, or UI. No photography, perspective, gradients, shadows, texture, glow, bevel, 3D, watermarks, stock clip art, or detailed illustrations.
Direction: an architectural uppercase A emblem. Build a bold, compact, slightly forward-moving A from two broad angular strokes with a deliberate right-angle, stepped negative-space counter, subtly referring to the 90 in the name. The A should feel engineered and have an immediately memorable silhouette. Make it unmistakably an A with a considered crossbar, rather than an ordinary hollow triangle or a mountain. Use few solid shapes and substantial negative space so it can survive at favicon size. Do not add rockets, planets, orbit rings, stars, circuitry, or neural-network dots.
Pair the emblem above a custom uppercase geometric sans-serif wordmark. Exact wordmark text: "ASTRO90" (A S T R O 9 0), seven characters, no spaces or punctuation. Strong medium-bold typography with a subtle angle or cut echoed from the emblem, while keeping the name immediately legible. Carefully kern the O90 sequence. Emblem and typography should have a strong visual relationship.

directions.title: Orbit 90
directions.prompt:
Use case: logo-brand.
Asset type: a professionally art-directed logo concept presentation for Astro90.com.
Brand context: Astro90 is the parent development studio behind Lighthouse, Inkube, Ktesio, Yanando, Heronis, and other products. It builds games, agentic AI software, and open-source software. The identity must have enough character for games and enough clarity for software and an umbrella studio.
Output: landscape 1536x1024 image, flat vector-like graphic design with crisp precise edges. Strictly black and white: solid black ink on pure white background. Restrained, original, confident identity design with generous white space and optically balanced proportions. This is a logo exploration, not a website or merchandise mockup.
Presentation layout: one generously sized main logo lockup centered in the upper 75 percent of the page. Along the bottom, present two discreet small-scale versions of the same emblem: solid black on white, and solid white on a solid black square. The small versions must reproduce the main emblem faithfully. Keep these supporting samples visually quiet and aligned. No headings, labels, explanatory text, slogans, color swatches, decorative lines, or UI. No photography, perspective, gradients, shadows, texture, glow, bevel, 3D, watermarks, stock clip art, or detailed illustrations.
Direction: a bold numeral monogram that fuses 9 and 0 into one compact orbital emblem. Design two closely integrated circular forms with generous open counters and a single decisive terminal that turns through 90 degrees. Both numerals must remain recognizable in the resulting 90 ligature. The silhouette should imply continuous movement and a studio creating its own worlds. Focus on the black shapes and distinctive negative space. Avoid a literal planet with a thin Saturn ring, an infinity symbol, a chain-link icon, a generic black circle, stars, rockets, sparkle motifs, and neural-network dots. Give the numeral design excellent optical balance and a strong solid silhouette.
Pair the emblem above a clean, calmly confident uppercase rounded geometric sans-serif wordmark. Exact wordmark text: "ASTRO90" (A S T R O 9 0), seven characters, no spaces or punctuation. Make the 90 in the wordmark easy to read and let the wordmark's O, 9 and 0 share the emblem's geometry.

directions.title: Pixel A
directions.prompt:
Use case: logo-brand.
Asset type: a professionally art-directed logo concept presentation for Astro90.com.
Brand context: Astro90 is the parent development studio behind Lighthouse, Inkube, Ktesio, Yanando, Heronis, and other products. It builds games, agentic AI software, and open-source software. The identity must have enough character for games and enough clarity for software and an umbrella studio.
Output: landscape 1536x1024 image, flat vector-like graphic design with crisp precise edges. Strictly black and white: solid black ink on pure white background. Restrained, original, confident identity design with generous white space and optically balanced proportions. This is a logo exploration, not a website or merchandise mockup.
Presentation layout: one generously sized main logo lockup centered in the upper 75 percent of the page. Along the bottom, present two discreet small-scale versions of the same emblem: solid black on white, and solid white on a solid black square. The small versions must reproduce the main emblem faithfully. Keep these supporting samples visually quiet and aligned. No headings, labels, explanatory text, slogans, color swatches, decorative lines, or UI. No photography, perspective, gradients, shadows, texture, glow, bevel, 3D, watermarks, stock clip art, or detailed illustrations.
Direction: a modular, pixel-built uppercase A emblem that gives Astro90 a playful maker and game-studio character. Construct a compact A on a coarse square grid from a small number of substantial interlocking stair-step blocks. Include an intentional square counter and a firm horizontal crossbar so it reads as A. Use simple continuous block shapes rather than lots of detached tiny pixels. The coarse pixel silhouette should have energy and unusual character while still being professionally restrained and working at small scale. It should suggest building with reusable components. No faces, game controllers, literal arcade cabinets, stars, AI sparkles, arrows, or generic space-invader mascot.
Pair the emblem above a custom uppercase robust sans-serif wordmark with gently squared forms and a few carefully chosen pixel-like cuts. Exact wordmark text: "ASTRO90" (A S T R O 9 0), seven characters, no spaces or punctuation. The wordmark should be highly readable and contemporary; avoid a fully jagged retro computer font. Make this a deliberate type design, not standard type under a clip-art symbol.

Use case: logo-brand.
Asset type: a professionally art-directed logo concept presentation for Astro90.com.
Brand context: Astro90 is the parent development studio behind Lighthouse, Inkube, Ktesio, Yanando, Heronis, and other products. It builds games, agentic AI software, and open-source software. The identity must have enough character for games and enough clarity for software and an umbrella studio.
Output: landscape 1536x1024 image, flat vector-like graphic design with crisp precise edges. Strictly black and white: solid black ink on pure white background. Restrained, original, confident identity design with generous white space and optically balanced proportions. This is a logo exploration, not a website or merchandise mockup.

The small versions must reproduce the main emblem faithfully. Keep these supporting samples visually quiet and aligned. No headings, labels, explanatory text, slogans, color swatches, decorative lines, or UI. No photography, perspective, gradients, shadows, texture, glow, bevel, 3D, watermarks, stock clip art, or detailed illustrations.
Direction: a typographic identity where the wordmark itself is the hero. Replace the usual emblem-above-name layout with one large, beautifully drawn custom lowercase wordmark centered in the upper 75 percent. Exact text: "astro90" (a s t r o 9 0), seven characters, no spaces or punctuation. Use a bold, warm, rounded grotesk with compact proportions, a single-storey a, and confident rhythm. Draw the a, o, 9 and 0 from related rounded-square geometry. Develop a subtle custom relationship between the terminal of the 9 and the contour of the 0 without making either unreadable. Aim for an independent creative engineering studio: accessible, assured, and distinctive. No decorative stars, planets, rockets, AI sparkles, gradients, circles around the whole name, or separate generic logo symbol.
For the two small bottom samples only, extract the same custom lowercase a from the wordmark as the standalone icon, black on white and reversed on the black square. The extracted letter must match the wordmark exactly. Put all the craft into the letterforms and optical spacing.
